co-question.1.t0.name: co-question.1.t3.eleven_v3
co-question.1.t0.text: So when does that money come back?

a1-lab.1.t0.name: a1-lab.1.t0.eleven_multilingual_v2
a1-lab.1.t0.text: This is a lab for money decisions. We run the numbers on public data and show every assumption.

a1-scope.1.t0.name: a1-scope.1.t2.eleven_v3
a1-scope.1.t0.text: US only, the rates here are history, not a forecast.

a1-rehook.1.t0.name: a1-rehook.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-rehook.1.t0.text: By the end, you will see the exact rate drop that pays back a refinance like Maya's within 36 months, and how every rate drop since 1971 actually played out.

a1-maya.1.t0.name: a1-maya.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-maya.1.t0.text: She borrowed $375 ,000 in October, 2023. The month, the 30 -year rate peaked.

a1-you.1.t0.name: a1-you.1.t2.eleven_v3
a1-you.1.t0.text: And if your own rate starts with a seven, the question is yours as well.

a1-median.1.t0.name: a1-median.1.t3.eleven_v3
a1-median.1.t0.text: No, in 2025, the median closing cost on a rate and term refinance was $5 ,124.

a1-hmda.1.t0.name: a1-hmda.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-hmda.1.t0.text: Lenders must report every mortgage they make and since 2018 the total loan costs of each one

a1-count.1.t0.name: a1-count.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-count.1.t0.text: That is the middle of 488 ,241 such loans that lenders reported under the Home Mortgage Disclosure Act.

a1-spread.1.t0.name: a1-spread.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-spread.1.t0.text: Half of those borrowers paid between $3 ,443 and $8 ,270.

a1-terms.1.t0.name: a1-terms.1.t2.eleven_v3
a1-terms.1.t0.text: The bill is the closing costs, origination charges, discount points, the appraisal, title insurance, and the rest.

a1-turn.1.t0.name: a1-turn.1.t1.eleven_v3
a1-turn.1.t0.text: But that bill barely grows with the loan, so it lands much harder on some borrowers than on others.

a1-dan.1.t0.name: a1-dan.1.t1.eleven_v3
a1-dan.1.t0.text: Take Dan, who borrowed $115 ,000 in the same month at the same rate.

a1-dan2.1.t0.name: a1-dan2.1.t2.eleven_v3
a1-dan2.1.t0.text: On loans under $150 ,000, the median bill was 3 .4 % of the amount borrowed.

a1-dan3.1.t0.name: a1-dan3.1.t2.eleven_v3
a1-dan3.1.t0.text: For Dan, that is $3 ,667, fewer dollars than Maya, but a far larger share of his loan.

a1-priya2.1.t0.name: a1-priya2.1.t2.eleven_v3
a1-priya2.1.t0.text: On loans of $750 ,000 and more, the bill was 0 .5%.

a1-priya3.1.t0.name: a1-priya3.1.t3.eleven_v3
a1-priya3.1.t0.text: For Priya, that is $5 ,034, about Maya's bill, on a loan nearly three times the size.

a1-save.1.t0.name: a1-save.1.t2.eleven_v3
a1-save.1.t0.text: what the bill buys is a lower payment. At today's rate, Maya's payment falls by $221 a month.

a1-rule.1.t0.name: a1-rule.1.t0.eleven_v3
a1-rule.1.t0.text: Divide the bill by that saving and you get the answer most calculators give, 24 months.

a1-payoff.1.t0.name: a1-payoff.1.t3.eleven_v3
a1-payoff.1.t0.text: By that count, the refinance has paid for itself, or has it?

a2-q.1.t0.name: a2-q.1.t1.eleven_v3
a2-q.1.t0.text: Here is what that division leaves out.

a2-old.1.t0.name: a2-old.1.t1.eleven_v3
a2-old.1.t0.text: Maya's old loan already has 35 payments behind it.

a2-reset.1.t0.name: a2-reset.1.t2.eleven_v3
a2-reset.1.t0.text: A refinance starts afresh 30 years. So the new loan pays the balance down more slowly than the old one would have.

a2-why.1.t0.name: a2-why.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-why.1.t0.text: Early payments are mostly interest. Maya's old loan was just starting to pay down real principal and the new one starts that schedule over.

a2-owe.1.t0.name: a2-owe.1.t2.eleven_v3
a2-owe.1.t0.text: So count what she still owes on each loan, month by month.

a2-gap.1.t0.name: a2-gap.1.t1.eleven_v3
a2-gap.1.t0.text: After 24 months, the new loan leaves her owing $1 ,133 more than the old one would have.

a2-real.1.t0.name: a2-real.1.t2.eleven_multilingual_v2
a2-real.1.t0.text: So, counting what she still owes? Break -even is not 24 months, it is 30.

a2-thesis.1.t0.name: a2-thesis.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-thesis.1.t0.text: Most calculators stop at the monthly saving. The balance keeps the score for longer.

a2-small.1.t0.name: a2-small.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-small.1.t0.text: The smaller the cut, the bigger that gap.

a2-s025.1.t0.name: a2-s025.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-s025.1.t0.text: At a cut of 0 .25 points, the division would promise 38 months.

a2-s025b.1.t0.name: a2-s025b.1.t2.eleven_v3
a2-s025b.1.t0.text: counting the balance. Maya never catches up before her old loan would have been paid off.

a2-cliff.1.t0.name: a2-cliff.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-cliff.1.t0.text: Below 0 .5 points, the fresh start can swallow the savings entirely.

a2-s10.1.t0.name: a2-s10.1.t3.eleven_v3
a2-s10.1.t0.text: At a cut of one point, the two answers nearly meet.

a2-s10b.1.t0.name: a2-s10b.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-s10b.1.t0.text: The division says 16 months, the balance says 18.

a2-dan.1.t0.name: a2-dan.1.t2.eleven_v3
a2-dan.1.t0.text: Now Dan, at today's rate, his payment falls by only $68 a month.

a2-dan2.1.t0.name: a2-dan2.1.t1.eleven_v3
a2-dan2.1.t0.text: The division says 55 months. Counting what he still owes, it is 75.

a2-dan3.1.t0.name: a2-dan3.1.t3.eleven_v3
a2-dan3.1.t0.text: If Dan sells after three years, the refinance leaves him $1 ,777 behind.

a2-dan4.1.t0.name: a2-dan4.1.t1.eleven_v3
a2-dan4.1.t0.text: After seven years, he is only $386 a head.

a2-priya.1.t0.name: a2-priya.1.t1.eleven_v3
a2-priya.1.t0.text: Priya saves $593 a month and is even after 11 months.

a2-priya2.1.t0.name: a2-priya2.1.t3.eleven_v3
a2-priya2.1.t0.text: If she sells after three years, she is $11 ,482 a head. After seven, $30 ,387.

a2-maya.1.t0.name: a2-maya.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-maya.1.t0.text: and Maya, the middle case, $1 ,039 ahead after three years, $8 ,093 after seven.

a2-sell.1.t0.name: a2-sell.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-sell.1.t0.text: Put another way, a house sold before the break -even month turns the refinance into a loss, and one kept past it turns it into a gain.

a2-payoff.1.t0.name: a2-payoff.1.t0.eleven_v3
a2-payoff.1.t0.text: Same rate, same month. The answer depends on the size of the loan, how old it is and how long the house is kept.

a3-q.1.t0.name: a3-q.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-q.1.t0.text: The division also assumes today's rate is the last one. What happened in the real drops?

a3-all.1.t0.name: a3-all.1.t3.eleven_v3
a3-all.1.t0.text: We found every fall of at least one point in the 30 year rate since 1971, 13 of them.

a3-rules.1.t0.name: a3-rules.1.t3.eleven_v3
a3-rules.1.t0.text: In each, someone like Maya borrows at the peak and refinances in the first month. The rate is one point lower.

a3-costs.1.t0.name: a3-costs.1.t3.eleven_v3
a3-costs.1.t0.text: closing costs use each year's median share. Before 2018, lenders did not report them. So a fixed share is used and marked illustrative.

a3-range.1.t0.name: a3-range.1.t2.eleven_v3
a3-range.1.t0.text: Counting what was still owed, break -even took between 10 and 20 months.

a3-simple.1.t0.name: a3-simple.1.t2.eleven_multilingual_v2
a3-simple.1.t0.text: The simple division would have said between 10 and 21.

a3-young.1.t0.name: a3-young.1.t1.eleven_v3
a3-young.1.t0.text: Nearly the same, because those loans were only months old when the rate fell, so the fresh start cost them little. Maya's loan is 35 payments old.

a3-81.1.t0.name: a3-81.1.t1.eleven_v3
a3-81.1.t0.text: The biggest fall began after the peak of 18 .63 % in 1981.

a3-81b.1.t0.name: a3-81b.1.t1.eleven_v3
a3-81b.1.t0.text: A refinance two months later paid back in 13 months, and the rate kept falling.

a3-priya.1.t0.name: a3-priya.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-priya.1.t0.text: for Priya's loan size, every one of those drops paid back within six months.

a3-dan.1.t0.name: a3-dan.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-dan.1.t0.text: For a loan like Dan's, with the bill a bigger share, the same drops took between 18 and 39 months.

a3-turn.1.t0.name: a3-turn.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-turn.1.t0.text: But in three of those drops, the rate fell another one point before the first refinance had paid for itself.

a3-twice.1.t0.name: a3-twice.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-twice.1.t0.text: Those borrowers met the same question twice, and a second refinance starts a new clock with a new bill.

a3-example.1.t0.name: a3-example.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-example.1.t0.text: In the drop that began in July 1984, the refinance came in November 1984.

a3-example2.1.t0.name: a3-example2.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-example2.1.t0.text: It needed 19 months to pay back. And the next drop of one point came seven months later.

a3-quiet.1.t0.name: a3-quiet.1.t3.eleven_v3
a3-quiet.1.t0.text: In the other 10, the first refinance was the one that mattered.

a3-23.1.t0.name: a3-23.1.t3.eleven_v3
a3-23.1.t0.text: Maya's own drop began in October, 2023. A cut of one point first arrived in August, 2024.

a3-23be.1.t0.name: a3-23be.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-23be.1.t0.text: refinancing then would have paid back in 19 months.

a3-answer.1.t0.name: a3-answer.1.t2.eleven_v3
a3-answer.1.t0.text: So, how far do rates have to fall before a refinance pays for itself?

a3-answer2.1.t0.name: a3-answer2.1.t3.eleven_v3
a3-answer2.1.t0.text: For a loan like Maya's, counting what is still owed, a cut of 0 .5 points pays it back within 36 months.

a3-today.1.t0.name: a3-today.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-today.1.t0.text: Today's cut is 0 .59 points. For Maya, that means ahead after 30 months and behind if the house is sold before then.

a3-limit.1.t0.name: a3-limit.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-limit.1.t0.text: That answer has limits. It leaves out taxes and any return on the cash, and it assumes the bill is paid upfront, not added to the loan.

a3-median.1.t0.name: a3-median.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-median.1.t0.text: It uses medians. Half of borrowers paid more than $5 ,124, and an offered rate can differ from the survey average.

a3-history.1.t0.name: a3-history.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-history.1.t0.text: And it is history, not a forecast. Nothing here says where rates go next.

a3-close.1.t0.name: a3-close.1.t0.eleven_v3
a3-close.1.t0.text: What history does show is the shape of the trade. A known bill upfront against savings and a balance that settle month by month.

m-rates.1.t0.name: m-rates.1.t3.eleven_v3
m-rates.1.t0.text: Method. Rates are Freddie Mac's weekly survey via Fred, checked against the optimal blue index since 2017.

m-drops.1.t0.name: m-drops.1.t1.eleven_v3
m-drops.1.t0.text: A drop counts when the monthly average falls at least one point, from a peak before rising one point from its low.

m-costs.1.t0.name: m-costs.1.t1.eleven_multilingual_v2
m-costs.1.t0.text: Costs are HMDA loan -level data from 2018 to 2025. Originated refinances, first lean, 30 -year term.

m-chars.1.t0.name: m-chars.1.t2.eleven_v3
m-chars.1.t0.text: Maya, Dan and Priya are illustrative. Each one's loan and bill are the medians for that loan size.

m-assume.1.t0.name: m-assume.1.t0.eleven_v3
m-assume.1.t0.text: Break -even counts, payment savings, plus the difference in balance still owed. Closing costs paid in cash, no taxes. Every figure is listed in the description.

o-recap.1.t0.name: o-recap.1.t1.eleven_v3
o-recap.1.t0.text: A small cut needs a long stay. A small loan needs a bigger cut. And the young loan loses less to the fresh start.

o-you.1.t0.name: o-you.1.t0.eleven_v3
o-you.1.t0.text: If the rate on your own statement starts with a seven, the same three questions apply. How big the cut, how old the loan, and how long the stay.

o-close.1.t0.name: o-close.1.t0.eleven_v3
o-close.1.t0.text: The monthly saving is only half of the answer. The other half, just as real, is what is still owed.

o-sources.1.t0.name: o-sources.1.t2.eleven_multilingual_v2
o-sources.1.t0.text: The sources are linked in the description, and the next decision is already on the bench.
